name: Joseph Murray
summary: American surgeon who performed the first successful human organ transplant and won the 1990 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

name: Charles Woods
summary: Burn patient treated by Murray at Valley Forge General Hospital during World War II.

name: James Barrett Brown
summary: Chief of surgery at Valley Forge General Hospital who shared experiences treating burn patients with Murray.

name: Thomas Gibson
summary: Researcher whose experiments on skin allograft rejection influenced Murray's understanding of immunologic processes.

name: Peter Medawar
summary: Researcher whose experiments on skin allograft rejection influenced Murray's understanding of immunologic processes.

name: Richard Herrick
summary: Patient with renal failure who received the first successful kidney transplant from his identical twin in 1954.

name: Ronald Herrick
summary: Healthy twin brother who donated a kidney to Richard Herrick in the first successful human kidney transplant.

name: J Hartwell Harrison
summary: Surgeon who led the donor's surgical team in the first successful kidney transplant.

name: John Riteris
summary: 24-year-old recipient of a kidney transplant between non-genetically identical twins who lived 29 years after the transplant.

name: Robert S Schwartz
summary: Researcher who used 6-mercaptopurine to prevent antibody production in rabbits, contributing to immunosuppression development.

name: William Dameshek
summary: Researcher who used 6-mercaptopurine to prevent antibody production in rabbits, contributing to immunosuppression development.

name: Roy Calne
summary: British researcher who developed azathioprine, a less toxic immunosuppressant used in kidney transplantation.

name: Mel Doucette
summary: 23-year-old patient who survived for over a year following the first successful renal allograft with immunosuppressive therapy.

name: Edward Donnall Thomas
summary: Co-recipient with Murray of the 1990 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for contributions to transplantation medicine.

name: Francis Moore
summary: Friend and colleague of Murray who commented on Murray's Nobel Prize achievement.

name: Leo Loeb
summary: Basic scientist who stated in his book that transplantation between individual humans would never be possible.

name: Siang Yong Tan
summary: Emeritus Professor of Medicine at University of Hawaii and author of this biographical article.

name: Jason Merchant
summary: Co-author of this biographical article about Joseph Murray.

name: Milford
summary: Town in Massachusetts where Joseph Murray was born.

name: Boston
summary: City in Massachusetts where Murray studied and worked at multiple institutions.

name: Pennsylvania
summary: US state where Valley Forge General Hospital was located.

name: College of the Holy Cross
summary: Small liberal arts college in Massachusetts where Murray attended undergraduate studies.

name: Harvard Medical School
summary: Medical school where Murray received his medical education.

name: Peter Bent Brigham Hospital
summary: Boston hospital where Murray did his surgical internship and later served as chief of transplant surgery.

name: Valley Forge General Hospital
summary: Major plastic surgery centre in Pennsylvania where Murray was stationed during World War II.

name: Boston Children's Hospital Medical Center
summary: Boston hospital where Murray became chief of plastic surgery in 1971.

name: International Renal Transplant Registry
summary: Registry established following the success of renal transplantation protocols.

name: The Nobel Foundation
summary: Organization that awards the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

name: University of Hawaii
summary: University where article authors Siang Yong Tan and Jason Merchant were affiliated.

name: The Biological Basis of Individuality
summary: Book by Dr Leo Loeb that stated transplantation between individual humans would never be possible.

name: Surgery of the Soul: Reflections on a Curious Career
summary: Murray's autobiography published in 2001 recounting his career and patient encounters.

name: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1990
summary: Nobel Prize awarded to Murray and Edward Donnall Thomas in 1990 for contributions to transplantation medicine.
